# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — Initial capability creation: address formulas, error strings, and precision
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - prompt.md: Added rules for Literal Values (Formula Writing cluster), Type Accuracy, and Error Handling (Excel Error Strings cluster).
    - prompt.md: Added Precision rule (Unnecessary Modification cluster).
    - prompt.md/task_template.md: Added Verification step to workflow and task contract (Empty Output Ranges cluster).
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix; why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Literal Values: Fixes 37378, 46897, etc. by forbidding formulas. Safe because passing tasks already use literal values.
    - Error Handling: Fixes 37456, 53647, etc. by preventing error strings. Safe because passing tasks don't write error strings.
    - Precision: Fixes 39046, 48527, etc. by forbidding unrequested changes. Safe because passing tasks are precise.
    - Verification: Fixes 227-40, 9569, etc. by requiring read-back check. Safe because passing tasks already do this or are simple enough to be correct.
- Building on prior RESULTS: This is the first iteration (empty seed).
- Refuted hypotheses: None.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: None targeted this iteration.
- Plateau signal: N/A.
- Focus next iteration: Evaluate the impact of these foundational rules and refine based on the remaining failures.

## Iteration cand_0002 — Strengthen literals, precision, types, and range scanning
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - prompt.md: Strengthened "Literal Values" (Formula Writing cluster) to explicitly require computing in Python first.
    - prompt.md: Tightened "Precision" rule (Over-Writing cluster) to forbid writing to unrequested cells and rewriting correct values.
    - prompt.md: Added casting constraint to "Type Accuracy" (Wrong Type cluster) to prevent automatic casting of strings.
    - prompt.md: Added "Scan" step to "Analyze" workflow (Missing Data cluster) to ensure the agent finds the full extent of data.
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix; why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Literal Values: Fixes 7902 by ensuring the agent writes the count result, not the formula. Safe as passing tasks already use literals.
    - Precision: Fixes 39046, 59595 by stopping the agent from changing correct values. Safe as passing tasks are precise.
    - Type Accuracy: Fixes 395-36 by preventing string -> int casting. Safe as passing tasks maintain types.
    - Range Scan: Fixes 395-36 by ensuring the agent doesn't assume the preview range is the full data range. Safe as it only adds a scanning step.
- Building on prior RESULTS: Built on cand_0001. Did not re-try any regressed tasks from cand_0001 (31628, 395-36, 48620, 59595) with the same approach; instead, used more specific rules (casting, scanning).
- Refuted hypotheses: None.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: Calculation/Logic errors (cluster 4) and general "Incorrect Value" (cluster 6) remain; these may require more specific logic examples or tool improvements if they persist.
- Plateau signal: N/A.
- Focus next iteration: Review if the "Scan" and "Casting" rules fixed 395-36 and if "Precision" stopped the over-writing in 39046/59595.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.650 Δ=+0.050 · fixed={31628, 39046, 55979, 6698, 7902} · broke={560-12, 59196, 80-42} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0002: ACCEPTED val=0.650 Δ=+0.050 -->

## Iteration cand_0003 — Targeted fixes for formula-strings, precision, and instruction misinterpretation
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - prompt.md: Tightened "Literal Values" to forbid strings starting with `=` and handle "how-to" queries by performing the action (Literal Formula Write cluster).
    - prompt.md: Added explicit warning that writing outside target range is a failure (Precision Violation cluster).
    - prompt.md: Added guidance on keeping strings as strings for IDs/codes (Type Mismatch cluster).
    - prompt.md: Added manual boundary check and prioritization of specific requests over defaults (Data Extent / Instruction Misinterpretation clusters).
    - task_template.md: Added a check for modifications outside the requested range to the verification step (Precision Violation cluster).
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix; why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Literal Values: Fixes 46897 by preventing the agent from writing an Excel formula as a string. Safe as passing tasks use literals.
    - Precision: Fixes 560-12, 50768 by preventing out-of-range writes. Safe as passing tasks are precise.
    - Type Accuracy: Fixes 560-12, 395-36 by preventing casting of string IDs to ints. Safe as passing tasks maintain types.
    - Analyze/Instruction: Fixes 48620 by encouraging the agent to follow specific "not first match" requests. Fixes 395-36, 80-42 by strengthening boundary scans. Safe as it only adds analysis depth.
    - Verification: Fixes 560-12 by requiring a range check. Safe as passing tasks are precise.
- Building on prior RESULTS: Built on cand_0002. Did not re-try the "Scan" rule from cand_0002 with the same wording; instead, added manual boundary check guidance and specific request prioritization.
- Refuted hypotheses: None.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: Calculation/Logic errors (e.g. 51-12, 43436) and complex multi-sheet consolidations (80-42) remain.
- Plateau signal: N/A.
- Focus next iteration: Tackle remaining logic/calculation errors and complex consolidations.
